newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish speaker calls special constitution session.
newsitem.headline: Polish speaker calls special constitution session.

text.p: Polish parliamentary speaker Jozef Zych on Wednesday called a National Assembly session for the second reading of the country's draft new constitution, which would replace a communist-era charter.

"Using powers bestowed upon me I called a National Assembly session (for both houses of parliament) from Febrary 24 to February 28 for the second reading of the draft constitition," Zych said in a public television address.
Urging compromise between all political powers, Zych also said that a nationwide referendum on the new constitution would most likely take place in June, 1997.

After the new constitution is passed by the joint parliamentary session, it would go to President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who has said he is unlikely to propose any major changes to the document and will quickly submit it to the third and final reading.

Parliamentarians have spent three years on the constitution draft, but if the new charter is not approved before general elections due this autumn, different parties might win the polls and work on the draft would begin afresh.

The new constitution guarantees free publicly-funded basic health care for all regardless of income and free education, although the draft admits the possibility of some charges for higher state education.
The presidency would be slightly weakened, with parliament allowed to overthrow the president's veto by three-fifths of votes in the lower house rather than the present two-thirds majority.
The president would also have less say on appointments in the foreign, defense and interior ministries.
